summary.headline: Allcargo Q4 FY26 revenue flat at INR514 crores while EBITDA rose 41% YoY to INR60 crores; FY26 EBITDA up 16% to INR233 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR514 crores, flat YoY and slightly below the prior quarter, while gross profit rose to INR154 crores from INR149 crores and EBITDA reached INR60 crores. For FY26, revenue grew 5% to INR2,058 crores and EBITDA grew 16% to INR233 crores, with margin improving to about 11%. Consultative Logistics (CL) was the growth engine at 17% full-year growth, while Express was broadly flat, with management repricing and exiting unprofitable customers. PAT remained low at about INR6 crores, which management attributed to exceptional items, and Allcargo Global's listing timeline was pushed out.

segments.name: Express (B2B surface and air)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR362 crores (+6% YoY) on 3 lakh MT at INR12,037/MT realisation; FY26 revenue INR1,442 crores (+2%). Growth driven by surface, with auto and engineering, pharma and diversified industries as the named sectors.

segments.name: Consultative Logistics (CL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR151 crores (+3% YoY); FY26 revenue INR615 crores (+17% YoY). Warehouse under management at 8 million sq ft as of March 2026; full truckload and in-plant services added, and warehouse space moved to an asset-operating-lease model from April 2025.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA and PBT to grow ahead of revenue in coming quarters, with integration now largely behind the company.
Management is 'very optimistic' about Q1 FY27 numbers and expects margin improvement from pricing actions and a volume pickup from March onwards.

Express pricing measures (metro congestion charge, next-round-of-zero rounding, AER charges on about 1,100 pin codes) are said to have lifted yield and RPKG; further fuel and cost pressures are being covered via pass-through and planned for Q1 and Q2 FY27.
Plan to add 0.5 million sq ft of warehouse space in FY27, largely on an asset-light basis.
Management did not commit to a specific Express growth rate for FY27, saying growth would be 'much better' than the prior year but without quantifying it.

Allcargo Global listing: SEBI and exchange approvals received; revised information memorandum with audited annual financials to be filed within about two weeks, with listing expected roughly one month later.
capex_capacity: Warehouse space under management at 8 million sq ft as of March 2026.
Pure-play 3PL warehouses moved to asset operating lease model from April 2025, conserving capex and cash.
Plan to add 0.5 million sq ft of warehouse space in FY27, largely asset-light.
Transportation vertical expanded in FY25; full truckload business started within CL, adding to revenue.
Management said industry white space norms apply and Allcargo is well below industry norms for white space in its running stock.
demand_pricing: Express RPKG improved over the last 6 months via GPI activity, metro congestion charge, next-round-of-zero weight rounding, and AER charges on about 1,100 difficult pin codes; pin code network expanded from 19,000 to 32,000.
Express management weeded out some non-profitable customers and recalibrated segments; revenue growth is running ahead of tonnage growth.
Management said volume trend is at par with industry, with pent-up demand seen from March and into April.
Fuel price hikes are covered by contractual diesel price hike (DPH) pass-through, published monthly on the company website.
Macro: E-way bills 140.6 million in March 2026 (+13% YoY); GST collections INR1.78 lakh crore (+8.2% YoY); IMF projects about 6.5% India GDP growth in FY27 per management.
CL serves top e-commerce and quick commerce players through sort, fulfilment and cross-dock centres; over 10 million packages per month handled in e-commerce/quick commerce.

qa_highlights.question: Expected listing date of Allcargo Global and reasons for delay.
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Punjabi said SEBI and both exchanges approved the listing two days earlier; the revised IM with audited annual financials will be filed within about two weeks, and listing is expected about a month after that.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the petrol and diesel price increase on growth and H1 FY27 margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Pareek said fuel cost is a pass-through under contracts; Ketan Kulkarni added that a transparent diesel price hike mechanism is published monthly, so the company sees no challenge.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend outlook and when PAT will improve, with PAT at INR6 crores.
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Pareek said PBT before exceptional items improved 96% in FY26 and this should show in the next quarter; dividend is a Board and shareholder decision, to be recommended at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: Split of post Ind AS EBITDA between Express and Contract Logistics.
qa_highlights.answer: Management referred to slide 22 and said Sanjay Punjabi would follow up offline; no figures were given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of EBITDA growth and sustainability of margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Pareek said gross profit rose 2% YoY on integration efficiencies, plus employee and other expense rationalisation drove the 16% EBITDA growth; CL grew strongly while Express was flat. Management expects margins to improve further in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Express volume flat in FY26 and the demand challenges, and expected acceleration.
qa_highlights.answer: Ketan Kulkarni said volume was up about 2% QoQ in Q4 and revenue rose faster than tonnage due to deliberate customer pruning and quality focus; no specific volume growth target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Growth drivers for Express and whether CL growth will continue.
qa_highlights.answer: Ketan Kulkarni named surface as the growth driver with auto and engineering, pharma and diversified industries as the key sectors; he declined to commit to similar CL growth but said Express growth would be much better than last year.

risks_watch: Fuel and cost pressures from the West Asia crisis and the fuel price hike; reliance on contractual pass-through mechanisms.
Express PAT still low at INR6 crores, with a large gap versus EBITDA; exceptional items need to be tracked.
Express growth quality versus volume: customer pruning could limit tonnage growth.
Allcargo Global listing timeline, which has already slipped from the previously stated Q4 FY26.
Split of Express versus CL EBITDA was not disclosed on the call, limiting segment-level margin tracking.
Management said it is cautious on the near-term outlook due to geopolitical conditions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, pricing and Q1 FY27, with a clear focus on profitable growth. Cautious on near-term macro and geopolitical conditions. Evasive on quantified FY27 Express growth, CL growth, PAT, dividend and segment EBITDA split.
key_quotes: So all these have had a positive impact on the yield and the RPKG over the last 6 months, and it has improved to a level that we are very, very comfortable now where we are with RPKG.
We are very optimistic about Q1 FY '27 numbers.
Only metrics for investors to track is the EBITDA improvement.
So it's a very transparent customer-friendly mechanism that we have.
